category: push notification API for iOS, Android and web browsers (hosted)

free_tier.stated: Beams Sandbox plan, priced Free: 1,000 subscribers (registered devices) and Standard support
free_tier.notes: A subscriber is a device registered to receive notifications. The count is the sum of concurrent subscribers across all Beams instances for a given day. A device counts from the SDK start call until the stop call, or until the platform gateway invalidates its token. Reinstalling an app on a device adds a new subscriber until the cleanup removes the old one. The pricing page names no notification count, and an older tutorial says a free plan can send unlimited push notifications to up to 1000 devices. The next plan is Startup at USD 29 a month for 10,000 subscribers.

per_object_cap.stated: 10 KiB request body on a publish to interests; 200 KiB request body on a publish to users
per_object_cap.notes: The two publish endpoints have different caps, so no single byte count is recorded. The body carries the target list and the payload for each platform.

retention.stated: An undelivered notification expires at the platform gateway after its time-to-live: at most 4 weeks on web push and FCM, and the payload expiration timestamp on APNs. A device registration stays until the SDK stop call or until the gateway invalidates the token
retention.notes: Web push accepts a time-to-live of at most 2419200 seconds and defaults to 4 weeks. FCM takes at most 4 weeks, which is also its default. APNs takes an expiration timestamp in the payload. 4 weeks is 28 days (4 x 7).

egress.terms: not stated: the pricing page lists subscribers and a support level and names no notification count, byte allowance or price per notification

interface_detail: Publish API: HTTPS POST to INSTANCE_ID.pushnotifications.pusher.com under /publish_api/v1/instances/INSTANCE_ID/publishes/interests or /publishes/users, with a JSON body and the instance secret key as a Bearer token. Devices register through the Android, iOS and Web SDKs, which call the Device API on the same host.
tooling: Official client SDKs for Android, iOS, Web (JavaScript) and Flutter; official server SDKs for Go, PHP, Node.js, Python, Java and Kotlin, Ruby and Swift; or any HTTP client that posts JSON with the instance secret key. A web page needs a service worker file, served over HTTPS, that imports the hosted Beams worker script.
chaining: A worker on any free compute service posts one HTTPS request to the Publish API to reach up to 1,000 registered browsers and phones, and Pusher Channels covers live updates to open pages.

limits.value: 1,000 subscribers (registered devices, counted as concurrent subscribers across all Beams instances for a given day)
100 requests per second to the Publish API; a request above the rate answers 429
10 KiB request body on a publish to interests; 200 KiB on a publish to users
notification time-to-live of at most 2419200 seconds (4 weeks) on web push and at most 4 weeks on FCM

limits_note: A publish to interests names 1 to 100 interests and a publish to users names 1 to 1000 user IDs. A device holds at most 5000 interests and a user holds at most 100 devices per platform. The vocabulary has no kind for a count cap, so the subscriber cap is filed as volume-quota.
binding_note: The 1,000-subscriber cap is the only plan threshold on the pricing page, and it counts registered devices, not bytes, so a growing app meets it before the Publish API rate of 100 requests a second.

identity_cost.detail: The Pusher sign-up form asks for an email address and a password, or a GitHub or Google sign-in, behind an invisible reCAPTCHA, and has no phone or card field; a Beams instance is then created in the dashboard. Android delivery needs an FCM service account file from a Firebase project, iOS delivery needs an APNs key from an Apple Developer account, and Safari delivery needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership. The web SDK guide for Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Opera uses only the instance ID and secret key from the dashboard.

reliability_note: Over the subscriber cap a publish answers 402 after a 7-day notice period and no notification is delivered, while device registration still succeeds; Standard support has best-effort response times, and the status page lists Beams and the Beams dashboard as Operational on 2026-11-01.
confidence_note: Every limit is quoted from first-party pricing, documentation and support pages. The Publish API host answered 405 to a GET on its POST-only route, and the hosted web service worker script answered 200. No notification was published, because publishing needs an instance ID and secret key, which only an account holds; a publish with a Sandbox key would move this record to measured. unverified: whether the first Beams instance asks for a card, how many instances a Sandbox account may hold and whether an idle Sandbox instance expires, because the Beams dashboard is behind a sign-up.
